P1.evidence: No setter named and no application read back, so P1a cannot apply. The frame ran two of four parts: 'I need to understand, like, what's your baseline? Like, where were you starting from and what you want to achieve, actually?' — where you are and where you want to go, with nothing on what is in the way or what you need. No frame agreement sought. The open question was clean and produced the prospect's full agenda unprompted, including his own price question: 'bring me up to speed. What's going on, and how can we actually help you?'

P2.evidence: Age, height and current weight were never asked and are absent from the record entirely — the only number in the file is the prospect's own volunteered 'I've probably gained around eight to 10 kilos.' Work was covered well and followed up on: 'is it more sitting at the desk kind of job?' then a walking-pad and standing-desk exchange. Health conditions asked only as limitations — 'but any conditions, like any stiffness in your hips, something like that?' — with nothing on hereditary risk. Injuries asked directly and the ankle surfaced with timing. Training week covered via 'what do you do? What have you been doing for the past?' Results from the current few weeks of kettlebell training were never asked. Diet covered thoroughly. Sleep and energy both never asked, which is a notable omission for a man with a two-month-old baby.

P3.evidence: Aesthetics approached through the gap to a former self rather than the scripted one-thing question: 'how far off do you feel that you are right, like from that physique that you had years back?' The mobility/strength/energy menu was never offered and the can't-do-physically question was never asked. The bridge and the moving-better question were merged into one future-pacing question that asked worth rather than driver: 'when you think about yourself, six months from now... What would that moment be worth to you?' Who-else-does-it-impact was approached by asking whether he had a wife and kids and then asserting the answer — 'Probably in a while we're going to be rolling on the floor with your son or daughter?' — rather than asking it. The legacy drive-through ran properly and the prospect took it further than the rep did: 'I need to be fit for him, for my family. And so, you know, when he grows up, I want to show him a good example.' The reflect-back was replaced by an assertion — 'every area of your life will improve... You will be a better husband, you will be a better parent' — with no confirmation sought.

P4.evidence: The strongest phase on the call and the strongest P4 in the batch. Past attempts established, then the rep refused to accept a vague cause and pushed twice. First: 'When you say life got in the way, what do you mean?' Then, after a hand-wave about marriage: 'Can I pause you for a second? I know you said you got married, but what? Specifically, what happened?' That single interruption produced the entire root cause — shared household complacency, takeaway, TV, the start-stop cycle, and the wife's parallel weight gain. He then went again on consistency: 'But how did that appear, like consistency? Like you didn't feel like going to the gym? Or what was the reason, actually?', which produced the real gap in the prospect's own words: 'it's probably the mindset that I had before... I want to train at this time and not at that time... that just adds to excuses.' Only the scripted 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own?' was absent.

P5.evidence: No two-year question and no 'why not?'. The settle question ran as a statement rather than a question, so the prospect agreed rather than argued the case himself: 'So I understand that staying at current level is not acceptable to you.' — 'Yeah.' The line-in-the-sand was replaced with an ownership question that landed well but does not carry the same weight: 'And ultimately, who's responsible to make this change?' — 'Myself.' — 'Good man. I thought you were going to say, it's Trevor's responsibility.' Consequence was never made concrete, which left nothing to push against when the prospect defaulted to sleeping on it.

P6.evidence: The belief question was never asked. The all-in question ran but produced an explicitly conditional yes: 'Are you fully committed to actually showing up and doing the necessary work to become that Maz that's showing up for your family?' — 'I would be, yes, but I think a big part of the decision-making process would just be to understand the costs around it.' The rep tried once to separate the two — 'I'm asking right now only for the commitment to showing up for the program' — got no cleaner answer, and presented the price anyway. The script requires returning to Phase 5 on hesitation; he went forward instead, and the conditional yes became the objection twenty seconds later.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted. Price and payment mechanics were explained, the prospect deferred, and the call moved to scheduling. Payment was never asked for, no link was sent, no onboarding call, agreement or welcome-email steps were reached.

objection_plays.detail: A textbook think-about-it landed — 'I would obviously have to think about it... I'll definitely have to think over it, and then let you guys know' — and not one OA move ran. No 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you there?', no 'what makes you feel it can?', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here', no 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now?'. The last of those was sitting right there: the prospect had just spent ten minutes describing a three-year start-stop cycle caused by deferring decisions, and the rep had already named it back to him. Instead the call went to calendar logistics.
The wife features heavily in the story but was never raised as a decision gate. The prospect framed it as his own call throughout.

The isolate ran correctly and got a clean answer: 'apart from the finances, anything else that would be stopping you from?' — 'I think it's just the finance side of things. Everything else looks good.' One financial probe ran: 'is it that you don't have the money right now, or is it tight, or you just feel that it's maybe too much?' The prospect answered with a rule rather than a fact and the rep let it stand. None of the financial picture ran — no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no credit cards, no available versus used credit, no investments — despite the prospect being an accountant who would have produced precise numbers. The break-it-up move ran early and unprompted, before any money objection had been made, which spent the option instead of trading it.
No timing objection. If anything the prospect argued the opposite, that the birth of his son made this the moment.
No fear or doubt about the method or his own ability to execute.

Script gap. The prospect named the rep's incentive to his face — 'I understand from where you're coming from, I get it. This is where your work is, and your job is to pitch and sell' — a trust-of-provider move that no play covers. It went entirely unaddressed; the rep's next line was about his own busy schedule, which reinforced rather than defused the framing.

notes: Outstanding root-cause work — the 'specifically, what happened?' interrupt is the single best discovery move in the batch and should be taught — then the whole call was given away at the back end. No belief question, a conditional yes accepted as a yes, price presented into that conditional yes, and then a clean think-about-it met with zero OA moves. Coach: never present into 'I would be, yes, but'; and when a prospect whose stated core problem is deferring and restarting says he needs to sleep on it, that is the exact moment the script's own line — the way you've been approaching this is what brought you here — is worth running.
